learningObjectives.title: Key characters (Macbeth, Lady Macbeth, Banquo, Macduff)

questions.q: How many witches confront Macbeth and Banquo on the heath at the start of the play?
questions.explain: The three witches (the Weird Sisters) meet Macbeth and Banquo in Act 1 and deliver their prophecies.

questions.q: After the opening battle, which title does King Duncan bestow on Macbeth?
questions.explain: Duncan rewards Macbeth with the title Thane of Cawdor after the previous thane is executed for treason.

questions.q: Whom does Macbeth murder in order to seize the throne of Scotland?
questions.explain: Macbeth kills the sleeping King Duncan at Inverness in Act 2 to make himself king.

questions.q: According to the witches, whose descendants are prophesied to become kings?
questions.explain: The witches tell Banquo he will 'get kings' though he is not one himself, prompting Macbeth's fear of him.

questions.q: Who kills Macbeth in the final act of the play?
questions.explain: Macduff, who was 'from his mother's womb untimely ripped', slays Macbeth and restores order.

questions.q: Whose wife and children does Macbeth order to be murdered?
questions.explain: Macbeth has Macduff's family slaughtered at Fife, an act of tyranny that hardens Macduff against him.

questions.q: Complete Macbeth's line: 'Is this a dagger which I see before me, the ___ toward my hand?'
questions.explain: Macbeth's hallucination of a dagger opens his Act 2 soliloquy before he murders Duncan.

questions.q: Which character cries 'Out, damned spot! out, I say!'?
questions.explain: Lady Macbeth speaks this during her sleepwalking scene as guilt over Duncan's murder overwhelms her.

questions.q: The witches' line 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair' most directly introduces which idea?
options: The beauty of the Scottish landscape
Appearance versus reality and moral disorder
questions.explain: The paradox signals a world where moral values are inverted and appearances deceive.

questions.q: Lady Macbeth's plea 'unsex me here' most clearly shows her desire to:
options: Cast off feminine compassion so she can help commit murder
Disguise herself as a man to escape
Protect her husband from the witches
questions.explain: She calls on spirits to strip away gentleness and fill her with cruelty to steel herself for Duncan's murder.

questions.q: When Macbeth admits he has 'no spur... but only vaulting ambition', what does this reveal?
options: He is being forced to act by the witches
Ambition is his only real motive for the murder
He loves Duncan too much to harm him
He believes the murder is justified by law
questions.explain: Macbeth recognises that no just cause drives him, only overreaching ambition that will destroy him.

questions.q: Macbeth's line 'Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood clean from my hand?' most strongly conveys:
options: His overwhelming guilt after murdering Duncan
questions.explain: The blood he cannot wash away symbolises guilt so great that no ocean could cleanse it.

questions.q: What is the dramatic function of Banquo's ghost appearing at the banquet?
options: To expose Macbeth's guilt and mental unravelling in public
To warn Scotland of an invasion
To reveal that Banquo is still alive
questions.explain: Only Macbeth sees the ghost, and his terrified reaction publicly betrays his disturbed conscience.

questions.q: Why does Shakespeare present Duncan and Malcolm as they are in the play?
options: To contrast good, rightful kingship with Macbeth's tyranny
To show that all kings are corrupt
To emphasise the power of the witches
questions.explain: Their virtue and legitimacy highlight, by contrast, the destructive tyranny of Macbeth's rule.

questions.q: Why does Shakespeare open the play with the witches?
options: To establish an atmosphere of evil and the supernatural from the start
To explain the history of Scotland's kings
To introduce the play's romantic plot
To reassure the audience that order will prevail
questions.explain: The eerie opening immediately creates a sense of disorder and supernatural menace that pervades the play.

questions.q: Lady Macbeth's advice to 'look like th' innocent flower, but be the serpent under't' encourages Macbeth to:
options: Hide murderous intent behind a welcoming appearance
questions.explain: She urges him to mask his deadly purpose with a friendly exterior, reinforcing the appearance-versus-reality theme.

questions.q: A student argues that Lady Macbeth is ultimately consumed by guilt. Which quotation best supports this?
options: 'Fair is foul, and foul is fair'
questions.explain: Her sleepwalking attempt to wash away imagined bloodstains dramatises her collapse under guilt.

questions.q: A student writes that ambition drives Macbeth to murder. Which quotation is the strongest evidence?
options: 'Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood clean'
'Fair is foul, and foul is fair'
questions.explain: This image directly names ambition as the overreaching force propelling Macbeth towards the murder.

questions.q: To analyse how Shakespeare presents the supernatural, which detail is most relevant?
options: The witches' chant 'Double, double toil and trouble'
Duncan naming Macbeth Thane of Cawdor
The banquet held for the thanes
questions.explain: The witches' incantation while brewing their charm is a key expression of the supernatural theme.

questions.q: A student wants to compare Macbeth against a model of good kingship. Which character best serves as that contrast?
questions.explain: Duncan's virtue, generosity and rightful rule stand as the ideal of kingship against which Macbeth's tyranny is measured.

specSource: AQA GCSE English Literature (8702) specification; Macbeth
